ledger.note: 1033: the County of Bar emerges from Upper Lorraine. Infobox: 'Established 1033', 'Divided from Lorraine 1033'; Sophia, who inherited on Frederick III's death in 1033, 'the first person to associate the comital title with Bar'. 'The county of Bar originated in the frontier fortress of Bar' built around 960. The page names no towns, so the department of Meuse is my reading of the county.

region.text: the county west of the Meuse, the Barrois mouvant

ledger.note: 1297: Philip IV invades Bar over Henry III's help to Edward I. Page: 'Philip IV invaded in 1297 over Henry III's aid to Edward I'. The page names no campaign zone; the county west of the Meuse is my reading, since it became the French fief.

region.text: the county west of the Meuse, the Barrois mouvant

ledger.note: 1301: the Treaty of Bruges ends Bar's war with Philip IV. 'The fighting ceased after the 1301 Treaty of Bruges'; 'Henry gave up some fortresses and paid homage to Philip for part of his lands', the Barrois mouvant ('Henry was forced to recognise all of his county west of the river Meuse as a fief of France', Duchy of Bar page). The war begins in 1297 ('Philip IV invaded in 1297').

1354: the Count of Bar takes the ducal title and becomes a peer of France. Page: 'the Count of Bar took the ducal title and was thereafter recognised as a Peer of France'; infobox 'Raised to a duchy 1354' (Père Anselme believed Count Robert was created duke by King John II).

1430: Duke Louis dies and Bar passes to René I of Anjou. Page: 'Louis died in 1430 and Bar passed to René I, who was married to Isabella, Duchess of Lorraine'; in 1431 the couple inherited Lorraine, so Bar and Lorraine have one ruler from then.

region.text: the County of Bar around Bar-le-Duc (the page lists no towns; the department of Meuse is my reading)

ledger.note: 1480: Bar is united with the Duchy of Lorraine under René II. Page: 'From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine'; infobox 'United with Lorraine 1480'.

region.text: Bar, united to the Duchy of Lorraine

ledger.note: 1480: the Duchy of Bar ends as a separate state in Lorraine (it passes to the French crown with Lorraine in 1766). 'From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine.'

wars.name: Philip IV's invasion of Bar

zones.text: the county west of the Meuse

wars.outcome: Philip IV invaded in 1297; by the Treaty of Bruges (1301) Henry III gave up some fortresses and held his county west of the Meuse as a fief of France (the Barrois mouvant); the east stayed imperial (the Barrois non-mouvant).
wars.note: Henry III was Edward I's ally ('When war broke out in short order between France and England, Henry was drawn in', Henry III page); the Gascon War article was not opened.

certainty.note: A frontier county with no boundary record on the pages.
The Meuse separates the French fief (Barrois mouvant) from the imperial east after the 1301 Treaty of Bruges; the line is the river, not a survey.

notes:
Written for eu-10-x from two pages (Duchy of Bar, Henry III Count of Bar); the second is thin (no towns, no terms beyond homage). Neither gives an area or a town list, so the whole state is drawn as the department of Meuse (Bar-le-Duc) in one keyframe from 1033 to 1479, a coarse reading: the county also held land east of the Meuse (Barrois non-mouvant) and the acquisitions of the 13th-15th centuries are not on the pages.
STATE END: the page lists a duchy of Bar to 1766, but the Duchy of Lorraine dossier (eu-09, duchy-of-lorraine) carries Bar from 1480 inside the united duchies, and Cliopatria's Duchy of Lorraine row (1431-1768) is the shape in those years; so this state ends in 1480 with a merge. For 1431-1479 the Lorraine dossier has Bar as a loss/gain to house-of-valois-anjou (René I's Anjou house), which this dossier does not contradict: 1431-1479 Bar is René's, not part of Lorraine's shape.
FOR THE KINGDOM OF FRANCE DOSSIER: the 1301 Treaty of Bruges made the county west of the Meuse a French fief (a vassal_start for duchy-of-bar in kingdom-of-france, absent there). The Bar page also gives 1301 'Divided between France and the Empire'.
PAGES SILENT ON: the 1033 land beyond Bar itself, the Pont-a-Mousson and Briey districts, the 1419 union (the page gives 1419 only as René's start in the regnal list), the date of Louis XI's involvement (the page names Peter II of Bourbon as regent in 1484), the rulers list (not read in full, so no rulers strip). The Meuse department is the only region name used.
